Novo Nordisk's Clinical Ledger: Retatrutide's Head-to-Head Win, a Pediatric Insulin Approval and the
stories.body:
Eli Lilly's Wednesday release of Phase 3 data for retatrutide has handed Novo Nordisk a direct clinical challenge in type-2 diabetes — one that a 2.7% share price gain on Friday does nothing to erase. The TRANSCEND-T2D-2 trial pitted Lilly's investigational candidate against Ozempic at a 2 mg dose in adults with type-2 diabetes, and the results favored the challenger on both of the study's headline measures.
After 80 weeks, patients on retatrutide recorded average weight loss of 20.9%, against 9.4% in the Ozempic arm. On glycaemic control, Lilly reported an A1C reduction of 2.2% with retatrutide versus 1.8% with Ozempic. What makes the comparison sting for Novo Nordisk is its architecture: the trial benchmarks a rival's pipeline asset squarely against one of the Danish company's own flagship products. Lilly's figures remain top-line Phase 3 data, not a regulatory verdict on retatrutide.
